candidates.requirement: Enable the supported INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE configuration so string parsing can invoke the name-only handler after an earlier parse error.
candidates.target_route: An accepted input such as `[broken\nname` reaches LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput, then ini_parse_string and ini_parse_stream; the first line records an error and the second is a no-value name.
candidates.failure_condition: The recipe supplies no enabling definition, so INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE defaults to 0 and the second line takes the error-only branch without invoking the handler.
candidates.alternative_paths: No input can enable a compile-time branch. The entry makes one parse-string call, and the recipe does not use the repository's enabling option.

candidates.requirement: Exercise a no-value handler refusal after an earlier error to cover preservation of the first error.
candidates.target_route: With no-value handling enabled, a finite input containing a malformed section followed by a name-only line reaches the changed handler-failure guard when the target callback returns 0 for that name.
candidates.failure_condition: The old recipe disables no-value handling, and the old callback returns 1 for every invocation, so the guard's handler-failure behavior is never reached.
candidates.alternative_paths: Other parser error assignments do not execute this changed guard. Natural input cannot change the callback's constant return value or the compile-time default.
